summary: chromacli ships a Windows dropper that fetches and executes an unsigned EXE from gofile.io after disabling Defender
details: The package presents itself as a terminal color library, but its exported API (Color.paint / print / __call__) contains an import-reachable Windows code path that downloads an unsigned executable from the anonymous file-sharing host gofile.io (https://store-eu-par-12.gofile.io/download/web/a2a60e90-dea4-4c6c-9a02-be5ede78dc08/solace.exe), writes it to %TEMP%\SolaceRuntime\solace.exe, and launches it detached via subprocess.Popen with DETACHED_PROCESS. Immediately before the drop, the code invokes PowerShell with -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass and CREATE_NO_WINDOW to call Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath for the SolaceRuntime folder and -ExclusionProcess for solace.exe, suppressing Microsoft Defender detection of the staged binary. The behavior is gated by os.name == 'nt' and has no connection to the package's stated color-printing purpose. The payload is unsigned, unverified, hosted on an anonymous share, and the Defender-exclusion-before-execute pattern is characteristic of Windows malware droppers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
